title: Uncle Joey's Sweet & Sour Kielbasa

items.body: Cut the kielbasa into ½ in coins, on a slight angle so they sit flat.
Optional, but worth the extra pan: brown the coins in a dry skillet over medium-high, in batches, until the cut faces take real color, 5–6 min. Pour off the fat.
Put the kielbasa coins in the slow cooker. Add the ketchup, the pineapple with all its juice, the brown sugar, mustard and Worcestershire. Stir once to coat.
Cover and cook on Low for 3–4 h, or on High for 2 h. Stir at the halfway mark if you happen to walk past.
Take the lid off for the last 30 min so the sauce thickens and turns glossy. It’s ready when a spoon pulled through leaves a track that holds for a second. Hold on Warm until serving.

nutritionSource: USDA FoodData Central: SR Legacy (juice-pack pineapple, brown sugar, yellow mustard) and Branded Foods labels (Hillshire Farm Polska Kielbasa 14 oz, 2 oz = 180 kcal, 520 mg, 7 g; Heinz). A dash of Worcestershire and the rice aren’t counted.
notes: Party batch, 20 servings on toothpicks: 3 lb kielbasa, 1 cup ketchup, 2 cans pineapple, 1 cup brown sugar, 2 tbsp mustard, 2 dashes Worcestershire. Same steps. Leave it in the slow cooker on Warm with toothpicks and small plates.
Serve over white rice or buttered egg noodles. Don’t drain the can; the juice is the sour half of the sauce. Too sweet? Add a splash of cider vinegar (not on the original card).
Better on day two. Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Freezes fine, though the pineapple softens.
